stemMd:
A bottling plant runs two machines. Machine P fills $1{,}200$ bottles per hour and Machine Q fills $800$ bottles per hour; each machine fills at its own constant rate the whole time it is running, and neither machine stops once started. On Tuesday the two machines together filled $25{,}600$ bottles, and Machine P ran for exactly $3$ hours longer than Machine Q.

In the column **Hours Machine Q ran**, select the number of hours Machine Q was running on Tuesday. In the column **Bottles filled by Machine P**, select the number of bottles Machine P filled on Tuesday. Make only one selection in each column.
instructionsMd: This is a Two-Part Analysis question. Two columns of choices are offered; select exactly one choice in each column. Credit is given only when both selections are correct.
explanationMd:
Put the unknown on the machine you are asked about, then write one equation for the total.

Let $q$ be the number of hours Machine Q ran. Machine P ran $q + 3$ hours. Bottles filled equals rate times time, so

$$1200(q + 3) + 800q = 25{,}600.$$

Expand and collect:

$$1200q + 3600 + 800q = 25{,}600 \;\Longrightarrow\; 2000q = 22{,}000 \;\Longrightarrow\; q = 11.$$

So **Machine Q ran $11$ hours**, and Machine P ran $11 + 3 = 14$ hours.

The second column asks only about Machine P's output:

$$1200 \times 14 = 16{,}800 \text{ bottles}.$$

**How to check this.** Compute the other machine's output and add: Machine Q filled $800 \times 11 = 8{,}800$ bottles, and $16{,}800 + 8{,}800 = 25{,}600$, which is exactly the total given. Both selections are confirmed by one addition.

**The transferable technique.** On a Two-Part Analysis item the two columns are almost never two independent puzzles. Here the second column is *dependent* on the first: once $q$ is known, the second answer is a single multiplication. Always solve the column that carries the unknown first, and then read the other column off it — trying to attack both columns at once is what makes these items feel slow. Also note the trap built into the stem: the $3$-hour difference belongs to Machine P, so $q$ is the *smaller* time. Writing "$P = q + 3$" explicitly, rather than carrying the relationship in your head, is what keeps the sign straight.

distractorRationale.hours-a: This subtracts the 3-hour gap a second time, from Machine Q's own 11 hours. The gap has already been used once, when Machine P's time was written as q + 3.
distractorRationale.hours-c: This is 25,600 divided by the combined rate of 2,000 bottles per hour, which assumes both machines ran for the same length of time. The stem says Machine P ran 3 hours longer.
distractorRationale.hours-d: This is Machine P's running time, not Machine Q's. The column asks for Q, which is the shorter of the two.
distractorRationale.hours-e: This adds the 3-hour gap to Machine P's 14 hours instead of recognising that 14 already includes it.
distractorRationale.bottles-a: This is Machine Q's output, 800 times 11 hours. The column asks for Machine P's output.
distractorRationale.bottles-b: This is half of 25,600, which splits the total evenly between the machines. They ran at different rates for different lengths of time, so an even split is not justified.
distractorRationale.bottles-c: This is 1,200 times 11, which applies Machine P's rate to Machine Q's running time and so forgets the extra 3 hours Machine P ran.
distractorRationale.bottles-e: This is 1,200 times 17, using the mistaken 17-hour figure for Machine P that comes from adding the 3-hour gap to P's time a second time.

accessibilityText: A Two-Part Analysis question. Machine P fills 1,200 bottles per hour and Machine Q fills 800 bottles per hour, each at a constant rate. Together they filled 25,600 bottles on Tuesday, and Machine P ran 3 hours longer than Machine Q. The first column, headed Hours Machine Q ran, offers 8, 11, 12.8, 14 and 17. The second column, headed Bottles filled by Machine P, offers 8,800; 12,800; 13,200; 16,800 and 20,400. One choice must be made in each column.

provenance.notes: Original item. The total of 25,600 was chosen to make the hours a whole number, and the two columns were given numerically disjoint option sets so that no choice in one column can be confused with a choice in the other.

independentSolve.workingNotes: Let q = Q's hours; 1200(q+3) + 800q = 25,600 gives 2000q = 22,000, q = 11 (hours-b). P ran 14 hours at 1,200/hour = 16,800 bottles (bottles-d); check 16,800 + 11 x 800 = 25,600. Distractor bottles-c (13,200) is Q's hours times P's rate and hours-c (12.8) is 25,600/2,000.

review.notes: Author solved the item and verified the pair by reconstructing the 25,600 total from the two machine outputs. Each distractor was traced back to a specific arithmetic or reading error. Awaiting blind independent solve before publication.
